newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reforms needed to lift German economy, jobs - BDI.
newsitem.headline: Reforms needed to lift German economy, jobs - BDI.

text.p: Germany's economy will not gain the strength to take on large numbers of unemployed workers without further reforms to the taxes and labour costs companies have to pay, an employers' group said on Monday.

Although growth in other countries was lifting prospects for German exports, high taxes, wages and social security contributions were restraining companies from adding jobs, the Federation of German Industry (BDI) said in a report.
In turn, record joblessness was dampening consumer demand and dashing any boost from domestic markets, BDI said.
"No impulse from private demand is to be expected in view of high unemployment," BDI said. "The economic rebound will not have the strength to lead to a turnaround in the jobs market."

BDI said exports were rising as economic activity picked up in other countries and the strengthening dollar lowered the cost of German exports, but the trend was one-sided. "The rebound is missing domestic demand," BDI said.
The group said employers needed to see Bonn following "a clear course" in financial policy toward reducing the costs companies bear when they hire workers.
Without social security and tax reductions, "an easing of the difficult labour market becomes less and less probable," BDI said.
